scenes.title: What is Data Observability?
scenes.subtitle: Understanding the health of your data
scenes.narration: Data observability is the practice of continuously monitoring the health of data so problems are detected before consumers are affected.

scenes.heading: Validation versus observability

left.heading: Validation
points: Pass or fail on each load

scenes.narration: Validation tests the rules you can anticipate and returns a clear pass or fail on every load. Observability instead watches how data behaves over time and flags deviations you never wrote a rule for. Together they cover both the known failures and the surprising ones.

scenes.heading: What observability tracks
bullets: Freshness: is data arriving on schedule?
Volume: is the row count in a normal range?
Schema: has the structure changed unexpectedly?
Distribution: are the values within expected patterns?
scenes.narration: Freshness monitoring answers whether data landed on time, since late data is often the first symptom of a broken pipeline. Volume tracking notices when row counts spike or collapse. Schema monitoring catches structural changes, and distribution monitoring flags shifts in the actual values.

scenes.heading: The observability loop
steps: Collect metadata and metrics on each run
Establish a baseline of normal behavior
Alert owners with context to investigate
scenes.narration: The loop begins by collecting metrics and metadata from every pipeline run automatically. Those measurements build a baseline that captures what normal looks like. When new runs deviate from that baseline, the system alerts the right owners with enough context to start investigating quickly.

scenes.text: Observability turns silent data failures into visible, actionable alerts before they reach the dashboard.
scenes.narration: Rather than waiting for a stakeholder to notice a wrong number, observability watches your data continuously and warns you first. It complements validation by catching the problems no rule anticipated.
